title: RaceLab — inspect the repair, keep the failures
disclosures: Actual Microsoft Edge UI interaction recordings and application stills, captured through Playwright in fresh contexts; preparation and model waiting omitted
Public explorer displays recorded evidence; local workbench independently re-executes the retained Meta proposal without new model calls
Pinned source adapters, real disposable SQLite and controlled process sequences; no whole-application or external delivery guarantee
Authored controls remain separate from new Meta lifecycle candidates; ownership checks execute inside candidate methods; repository checks are not human feedback

Twelve planned arms attempted once across amended study and explicitly disclosed post-hoc continuation; feedback6/6 and direct4/6 complete-arm held-out passes; original setup and truncation retained; no general AI superiority claim
Generic synthetic English narration using Microsoft Zira Desktop
New RaceLab work by Tang Vu reuses earlier event transport, budget and local infrastructure; TEND, OpenMusic and airules are pre-existing inputs

scenes.heading: A lost job. A checked repair.
scenes.caption: Actual UI interaction / recorded TEND evidence / A fails → retained Meta B passes / new RaceLab work; earlier TEND and event infrastructure
scenes.narration: A worker saved this claim, then stopped. The original leaves zero completions. Switch to the retained Meta candidate: the job recovers, and the check passes. This is RaceLab, built by Tang Vu with Meta. TEND and the event infrastructure are earlier inputs.

scenes.heading: Run the exact source. Check the contract.
scenes.caption: Pinned MIT TEND method / QuickJS / real child processes and SQLite / original adapter has a fixed fixture completion guard
scenes.narration: The local workbench verifies a pinned public source revision. It executes the extracted TypeScript claim method in Quick J S, through a bounded bridge to real SQLite. Without interruption, the original works. The sixty second lease contract and this adapter's fixed completion guard are RaceLab additions, not upstream application guarantees.

scenes.heading: Follow the committed state.
scenes.caption: Actual process exit observed before replacement / saved SQL receipts / scrubber shows committed snapshots, not future state
scenes.narration: Step through the saved execution. Worker A claims the row and commits. RaceLab terminates that actual process and observes its exit. Worker B opens the same database after expiry. The original query ignores claimed rows. The job remains stuck. The candidate adds expired lease recovery. These are finite controlled sequences, not every possible schedule.

scenes.heading: Meta proposes. Independent checks decide.
scenes.caption: Public hypothesis → failed probe → candidate diff → independent checks / retained original: 2 requests, $0.015165
scenes.narration: Open the public investigation. Here is Meta's retained hypothesis, the requested crash probe, and the executed failure. Then inspect its candidate diff and independent checks. This original investigation used two requests and one candidate. The recording does not contain a complete raw transcript. The page exposes public artifacts, never hidden reasoning, and keeps the failure beside the repair.

scenes.heading: Make the ownership checks executable.
scenes.caption: New lifecycle adapter / first feedback candidate: 10/10 development + held-out / real contention, commit interruption, renewal and stale tokens
scenes.narration: The lifecycle adapter puts claim, renewal and completion ownership checks inside candidate methods. The first feedback candidate passes all ten conditions: competing workers, interruption before and after commit, long job renewal and old token rejection. Its authored control stays separate. This bounded adapter does not repair upstream completion or guarantee external delivery.

scenes.heading: Broader inputs. Retain the negative result.
scenes.caption: Pinned public inputs / OpenMusic: 14 checks pass / airules: 6 of 8 meet RaceLab's added line-edit contract / bounded adapters
scenes.narration: Two more public repositories widen the inputs. Unchanged OpenMusic code passes fourteen memory adapter checks. The airules diff function fails two of eight conditions under RaceLab's added line edit contract. That is a contract mismatch, not a concurrency finding. These bounded checks are not full application tests or human feedback.

scenes.heading: Measure it. Keep every failure.
scenes.caption: 12 arms attempted once / feedback 6 of 6; direct 4 of 6 / seven first-time arms in a disclosed post-hoc continuation / no general superiority claim
scenes.narration: Across twelve arms, feedback passes in six attempts; direct repair, four. Direct failures include truncation and an invented SQL column. Seven previously unrun arms were collected under a separately frozen continuation after the stop. No failed attempt was retried. This small collection does not establish general superiority.

scenes.heading: Inspect online. Recompute locally.
scenes.caption: Public recorded explorer / A/B, conditions, trace controls, actual/expected / unchanged evidence download / keyless local execution
scenes.narration: Anyone can inspect the public recorded explorer, select conditions, compare methods, and scrub the trace. Download the unchanged evidence, then run the local workbench to recompute it without a model key. RaceLab makes a repair reviewable: source, hypothesis, execution, failure, and a clear boundary around what passed.
